text: After reporting a leverage ratio, as defined in the agreements, of 1.75x at December 31, 2025, Elis is well in compliance with the covenant ratio. [#6797](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6797)
These financing contracts include, in particular: a leverage ratio <3.75 covenant(1) to be respected at the end of each half. [#6077](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6077)
This loan agreement contains, in particular: a leverage ratio <3.75 covenant(1) to be respected at the end of each half. [#6106](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6106)

Financing agreements The bank financing and private placement agreements described in Note 8.3 "Gross debt" to the 2025 consolidated financial statements, which can be found in chapter 5 "Financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025" of this Universal Registration Document, contain clauses requiring Elis to (i) comply with a financial covenant each half-year according to which the ratio of net debt as defined in the agreement to EBITDA (pro forma) after synergies (total net leverage ratio) is less than 3.75x at December 31, 2025 and on subsequent half-yearly test dates, and (ii) provide lenders with certain guarantees, in keeping with market standards, notably: a negative pledge whereby the borrower undertakes not to provide collateral to third parties, subject to certain exceptions; cross-default clauses stipulating that an event of default on any other borrowing would also render these agreements immediately due and payable; a periodic reporting obligation; compliance with legislation in force; and no change in control (resulting from the acquisition by one or more persons acting in concert of more than 50% of the voting rights in the Company). [#6796](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6796)
As at December 31, 2025, the total net leverage ratio was 1.75x. [#2079](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-2079)

The financial commitments include an obligation for the Group to satisfy a financial covenant as presented in Note 10.1 "Capital management." [#5998](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-5998)

As a result, as at December 31, 2025, the weighted average residual maturity of borrowings and gross financial debt was 3.1 years, with a long-term debt ratio (borrowings and gross financial debt maturing in more than one year/total borrowings and gross financial debt) of 78%; the use of bank loans and bonds to diversify its sources of liquidity and creditors: in order to benefit from economies of scale and facilitate access to financing on the capital markets (bonds and commercial paper), the Group centralizes the vast majority of its financing transactions through Elis; continuously maintaining a significant buffer of undrawn confirmed credit lines to secure liquidity and meet its short-term debt obligations, especially on its commercial paper program in case of capital market closures. [#6001](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6001)

10.1 Share capital and reserves Capital management The policy for allocating the Group's capital aims to improve shareholder returns by: pursuing new bolt-on acquisitions, with an acquisition budget of between 50 and 150 million per year(1); maintaining the investment grade status of Elis and continuing the reduction in financial leverage(2), but with a limit of approximately 0.1x per year; in this regard, financial leverage amounts to 1.75x as at December 31, 2025 (1.85x as at December The remaining cash will mainly be used to improve shareholder return, by means of paying a dividend or a share buyback. [#6184](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6184)

At the same time, our debt ratio reached a historic low of 1.75x as at December 31, 2025, illustrating the Group's solid financial structure. [#5303](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-5303)

Failure to comply with this covenant on the relevant date would constitute an event of default, which could entail the immediate payment and early redemption of some or all of the bonds issued under the USPP financing; a cross-default event, as explained above. [#6078](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000259591248-6078)
